title: New Year Hangover? 7 Expert-Approved Ways To Feel Better
text:
New Year Hangover? 7 Expert-Approved Ways To Feel Better
Hangovers can be rough, but they don’t have to be. Follow these simple cures to bounce back after the New Year 2026 party.
New Year’s parties are a fun way to bid adieu to the past year, but we’ve all been there: you wake up after a night of drinking, and your body feels like it’s been through a storm. Head pounding, stomach upset, mouth dry, energy gone, a hangover is your body’s way of signalling that alcohol has taken a toll. While no magic potion instantly wipes it away, there are practical steps you can take to ease the discomfort and help your body recover more smoothly.
Here are 7 ways to cure and soothe hangovers after New Year’s Eve party, as per Harvard Health.
Recommended Stories
1. Rehydrate Thoughtfully
One of the biggest problems after drinking is dehydration. Alcohol makes your body lose more water than usual because it suppresses the hormones that help your kidneys retain fluids. The result? You urinate more and wake up thirsty, tired and foggy. The best thing you can do first thing in the morning is drink water or a rehydration drink. Electrolyte-rich options, whether homemade (like coconut water) or store-bought, help replace sodium, potassium, and other minerals lost overnight, which can ease headache and fatigue.
2. Eat Something Light and Sustaining
When you drink alcohol, your blood sugar can dip, leaving you feeling weak and drained. Eating a simple breakfast- like toast, fruit, eggs, or broth- can raise your blood sugar slowly and give your brain the fuel it needs to function again.
Carbohydrates are especially helpful because they are easy for your body to process and can bring your energy levels back to normal without upsetting an already sensitive stomach.
3. Be Smart With Pain Relief
A throbbing headache is one of the hallmark hangover symptoms, and over-the-counter pain relief can help. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) such as aspirin or ibuprofen work better for this than acetaminophen.
These should be used carefully, especially if your stomach is already irritated or if you have liver concerns. Alcohol and acetaminophen together can strain the liver, so avoid acetaminophen until you’re fully sober.
4. Sip Tea or Coffee
Caffeine won’t cure a hangover, but a modest cup of coffee or tea can help clear the fog and give you a little mental lift. Keep in mind, though, that caffeine is a mild diuretic, meaning it can make dehydration worse if you haven’t been drinking fluids. Pair your tea or coffee with plenty of water to counter this effect.
5. Rest Until You Recharge
A hangover isn’t just a physical issue; it’s also a sleep quality issue. Alcohol disrupts normal sleep cycles, so even if you slept for a long time, it might have been fragmented and unrefreshing. Permitting yourself to sleep longer, take a mid-day nap, or just relax in a quiet space can significantly reduce grogginess and help your nervous system settle down.
6. Don’t Fall for “Hair of the Dog"
You might have heard people suggest drinking more alcohol to ease a hangover, a trick known as hair of the dog. It may dull symptoms briefly, but it only delays your body’s recovery and can make dehydration and other effects worse. True recovery comes from letting your body process the alcohol it has already consumed, not adding more to the mix.
7. Support Your Body With Vitamins and Minerals
Some research suggests that nutrients like B vitamins and zinc might lessen hangover severity when your diet includes them before and after drinking. While supplements aren’t a guaranteed fix and should be approached cautiously, incorporating foods rich in these nutrients- such as eggs, leafy greens, nuts and seeds – can support your body’s normal repair processes.
